claims.text: The low-field magnetocaloric response of non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films and nanoribbons is predominantly controlled by short-range atomic ordering and grain-boundary crystallinity.
Magnetic hysteresis in these films and nanoribbons is predominantly controlled by short-range atomic ordering and grain-boundary crystallinity.
Rapid thermal annealing enhances atomic ordering and grain-boundary crystallinity.
Enhanced structural ordering reduces magnetic-domain pinning.
Enhanced structural ordering improves local heat-transfer efficiency.
Reduced domain pinning and improved local heat transfer sharpen the magnetocaloric transition.
Reduced domain pinning and improved local heat transfer reduce magnetic hysteresis.
The as-deposited films and nanoribbons contain randomly distributed elements.
The as-deposited films and nanoribbons have disordered or suboptimally crystalline grain boundaries.
Disordered regions act as magnetic pinning sites.
Improved atomic and grain-boundary order produces more spatially uniform magnetic transitions.
Rapid thermal annealing at approximately 500 degrees Celsius for 5 seconds is expected to be near optimal.
Appropriately selected rapid thermal annealing can enhance ordering without significantly altering the material's nanoscale features.
Optimally annealed samples will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will produce a larger temperature change per low-field magnetic cycle than the as-deposited baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
A high-thermal-conductivity substrate will minimize heat-transfer limitations during low-field magnetic-cooling tests.
The proposed mechanism is intended to apply in thin-film or nanoribbon geometries at applied fields of 0.05 to 0.1 T.
The proposed annealing window is 400 to 600 degrees Celsius with dwell times of 1 to 10 seconds in argon.
The magnitude of magnetocaloric improvement may vary with composition and microstructural features not fully controlled by short-duration annealing.
